parts.title: Campus Conversation: The Campus Shuttle Bus
script: Narrator
Listen to a conversation between a student and a campus information desk worker.
Woman
Excuse me. Does this campus have a shuttle bus?
Man
Yes, we do. The campus shuttle runs between the dorms, the library, and the science building.
Woman
Great. I live in Oak Hall. How often does the bus come?
Man
On weekdays it comes every fifteen minutes. On weekends it comes every thirty minutes.
Woman
That helps. What time does the first bus leave in the morning?
Man
The first bus leaves at seven thirty in the morning. The last bus leaves at ten at night.
Woman
Is the shuttle free for students?
Man
Yes. Just show your student ID when you get on. No ticket is needed.
Woman
Perfect. Where do I wait near Oak Hall?
Man
There is a blue bus stop sign in front of the dorm. Wait there. The bus has the words Campus Shuttle on the side.
Woman
One more question. Can I bring a large backpack on the bus?
Man
Yes, backpacks are fine. Just keep the aisle clear so other students can walk past.
Woman
Thanks! I'll catch the bus tomorrow morning.
Man
You're welcome. Have a good day.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
questions.exp: The student asks about the campus shuttle and how to use it.

questions.q: How often does the shuttle run on weekdays?
questions.exp: The man says on weekdays it comes every fifteen minutes.

questions.q: What time does the first bus leave?
questions.exp: He says the first bus leaves at seven thirty in the morning.

questions.q: Listen again: "Just show your student ID when you get on." Why does the man say this?
o: To explain how students ride for free
To say the bus is closed today
To ask the student to buy a ticket
To tell her to leave campus
questions.exp: He is explaining that the shuttle is free if you show your student ID.

questions.q: Where should the student wait near Oak Hall?
o: At a blue bus stop sign in front of the dorm
questions.exp: He says there is a blue bus stop sign in front of the dorm.

questions.q: What will the student probably do tomorrow morning?
o: Drive her own car to class
Ride the campus shuttle from Oak Hall
questions.exp: She says she will catch the bus tomorrow morning after learning where to wait.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: How Do Rainbows Form?
script: Narrator
Listen to part of a lecture in a science class.
Professor
Good morning. Today we will talk about rainbows. Have you ever wondered why a rainbow appears after rain?
Professor
A rainbow needs two things: sunlight and water drops in the air. After a rain shower, many tiny drops of water stay in the air. When the Sun comes out, its light hits those drops.
Professor
Sunlight looks white, but it is really made of many colors mixed together. When sunlight enters a water drop, the light bends and splits into those colors. This splitting is called refraction.
Professor
Inside the drop, the light also reflects, or bounces, off the back of the drop. Then it leaves the drop and travels to your eyes. That is when you see the band of colors.
Professor
The order of the colors is always the same. Red is on the outside of the bow, and violet is on the inside. In between you see orange, yellow, green, and blue.
Professor
Here is an important tip. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the Sun behind you and the rain or mist in front of you. If you face the Sun, you will not see the rainbow.
Professor
Sometimes you can see a second, fainter rainbow above the first one. That happens when light reflects twice inside the drop. The colors in the second rainbow are in reverse order.
Professor
So remember: sunlight plus water drops, light that bends and reflects, and the Sun behind you. That is how a rainbow forms. Next time we will talk about why the sky looks different at sunset.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
questions.exp: The professor says today we will talk about rainbows and how they appear.

questions.q: What two things does a rainbow need?
o: Sunlight and water drops in the air
questions.exp: She says a rainbow needs sunlight and water drops in the air.

questions.q: What is refraction in this lecture?
o: When light bends and splits into colors
When rain falls to the ground
questions.exp: She says when sunlight enters a water drop, it bends and splits into colors, and that splitting is called refraction.

questions.q: Which color is on the outside of a rainbow?
questions.exp: She says red is on the outside of the bow, and violet is on the inside.

questions.q: Listen again: "If you face the Sun, you will not see the rainbow." Why does the professor say this?
o: To warn students never to go outside
To explain the correct position for seeing a rainbow
To say rainbows only appear at night
questions.exp: She is teaching that you need the Sun behind you, so facing the Sun means you will miss the rainbow.

questions.q: How does the professor organize the lecture?
o: She tells a long story about a camping trip
She explains what a rainbow needs, how light changes in a drop, then how to stand to see one
She compares rainbows to snowflakes only
questions.exp: She moves from sunlight and water drops, to bending and reflecting light, to where you should stand, then mentions a second rainbow.
